steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On September 30, 2026, Eastern Time is in Daylight Saving Time (EDT, UTC-4), and Madrid is in Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2). 

Madrid is 6 hours ahead of Eastern Daylight Time. 
Adding 6 hours to 5:00 PM (17:00) gives 11:00 PM (23:00) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time zone (PET), which operates at UTC-5 year-round with no daylight saving time. 

Subtracting 5 hours from 12:00 UTC on July 15, 2026 gives 07:00 on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST (Central European Summer Time) is UTC+2, while Tokyo's local time (JST) is UTC+9. Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST. 

Adding 7 hours to 9:00 AM on June 1, 2026 results in 4:00 PM (16:00) on June 1, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find the deadline in your local time in Madrid:

1. **PDT (Pacific Daylight Time)** is UTC−7.
2. On October 11, 2026, Madrid is observing **CEST (Central European Summer Time)**, which is UTC+2 (daylight saving time ends on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026).
3. The time difference is: $\text{UTC}+2 - (\text{UTC}-7) = +9\text{ hours}$.
4. Adding 9 hours to October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM (23:59) PDT gives October 12, 2026 at 08:59 CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. **PST (Pacific Standard Time)** is UTC−8.
2. In early March, Spain observes **CET (Central European Time)**, which is UTC+1.
3. Madrid is therefore 9 hours ahead of PST.
4. Adding 9 hours to March 3, 2026, at 11:59 PM (23:59) brings the time to March 4, 2026, at 08:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Central European Time (CET) is UTC+1, and Los Angeles is in Pacific Standard Time (PST, UTC-8) in February. This means Los Angeles is 9 hours behind CET.

Subtracting 9 hours from 10:00 AM on February 2, 2026 gives 1:00 AM on February 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Japan Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9, while Lima, Peru is in Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5 with no daylight saving time. 

This makes Lima 14 hours behind JST:
- May 5, 2026, at 08:00 JST minus 14 hours is May 4, 2026, at 18:00 PET.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 28, 2026, Pacific Time is in Daylight Saving Time (PDT, UTC-7). 
Spain switches from CEST to CET (UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). Thus, Madrid is 8 hours ahead of Pacific Time (UTC-7 to UTC+1).

Adding 8 hours to October 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM (23:59) gives October 29, 2026, at 07:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 30, 2026, Eastern Time is in Daylight Saving Time (EDT, UTC-4), so 9:00 AM EDT corresponds to 13:00 UTC. 

Madrid, Spain will have already switched to standard time (CET, UTC+1) on Sunday, October 25, 2026. Adding 1 hour to 13:00 UTC gives 14:00 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find the deadline in New York local time:

1. **Europe Daylight Saving Time:** In 2026, Daylight Saving Time in Europe ends on Sunday, October 25, 2026. Therefore, on October 27, 2026, Central European Time (CET) is UTC+1.
2. **New York Daylight Saving Time:** In the United States, Daylight Saving Time ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026. Therefore, on October 27, 2026, New York is still on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4.
3. **Conversion:** 
   - 18:00 CET = 17:00 UTC
   - 17:00 UTC = 13:00 EDT (UTC-4)

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid:

1. **Pacific Time (PT):** In the United States, Daylight Saving Time ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026. Thus, on November 2, 2026, PT is Pacific Standard Time (PST, UTC-8).
2. **Madrid Time:** Daylight Saving Time in Spain ends on Sunday, October 25, 2026. By November 2, Madrid is on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).
3. **Difference:** Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PST (UTC+1 vs. UTC-8).

Adding 9 hours to November 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM (23:59) PST gives November 3, 2026, at 08:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 20, 2026, the US is observing Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7), while Madrid is observing Central European Time (CET, UTC+1), as European daylight saving time does not begin until March 29, 2026. 

Madrid is therefore 8 hours ahead of PT. Adding 8 hours to March 20, 2026, at 11:59 PM yields March 21, 2026, at 7:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the webinar start time to your local time in Los Angeles:

1. **Webinar Time in CET:** March 25, 2026, at 12:00 PM CET. 
   - Daylight saving time in Europe does not begin until March 29, 2026, so Central European Time (CET) is UTC+1.
   - 12:00 PM CET corresponds to 11:00 UTC.

2. **Los Angeles Time:**
   - Daylight saving time in the United States begins on March 8, 2026, so Los Angeles will be on Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7.
   - 11:00 UTC minus 7 hours is 04:00 AM PDT on March 25, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 12, 2026, both the US and Spain are observing Daylight Saving Time:
- US Eastern Time is in Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4.
- Madrid is in Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

Madrid is 6 hours ahead of Eastern Time. Adding 6 hours to 12:00 AM (00:00) on October 12, 2026, gives 06:00 on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline from Anywhere on Earth (AoE) to your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. AoE corresponds to the UTC-12 time zone: October 9, 2026, at 23:59 AoE is October 10, 2026, at 11:59 UTC.
2. In October 2026, Madrid observes Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2 (14 hours ahead of AoE).
3. Adding 14 hours to October 9, 2026, 23:59 results in October 10, 2026, at 13:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On August 14, 2026, Pacific Time is in Daylight Saving Time (PDT, UTC-7), and Madrid is in Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2). The difference between PDT and CEST is 9 hours ahead.

12:00 PM PDT (noon) + 9 hours = 21:00 (9:00 PM) CEST on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Indian Standard Time (IST) is UTC+5:30. 
On November 10, 2026, Madrid is on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1.

The difference is 4 hours and 30 minutes behind IST:
11:59 PM (23:59) minus 4 hours and 30 minutes = 7:29 PM (19:29) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal Time (NPT) is UTC+5:45 (Nepal does not observe daylight saving time).
Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time zone (PET), which is UTC-5 (Peru does not observe daylight saving time).

1. 5:00 PM (17:00) NPT on April 2, 2026 converted to UTC:
   17:00 - 5 hours 45 minutes = 11:15 UTC (April 2, 2026).
2. 11:15 UTC converted to Lima, Peru time (UTC-5):
   11:15 - 5 hours = 06:15 (April 2, 2026).

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid time:

1. **Adelaide Time Zone on October 6, 2026:** South Australia observes Daylight Saving Time starting on the first Sunday of October (October 4, 2026). Thus, on October 6, Adelaide is on Australian Central Daylight Time (ACDT), which is **UTC+10:30**.
2. **Madrid Time Zone on October 6, 2026:** Spain is on Central European Summer Time (CEST) until the last Sunday in October, which is **UTC+2:00**.
3. **Difference:** Adelaide is 8 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Madrid.
4. **Conversion:** Subtracting 8 hours and 30 minutes from 10:00 AM on October 6 gives 01:30 AM on October 6.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 3, 2026:
- Sydney, Australia is still on Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST, UTC+10), as daylight saving time does not begin until the first Sunday in October (October 4, 2026). 
- Madrid, Spain is on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2).

Sydney is 8 hours ahead of Madrid. Subtracting 8 hours from 6:00 PM (18:00) gives 10:00 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
